plainLanguage: Tyler builds to the 2021 International Residential Code with its own local changes (city code Sec. 6-151), plus the 2021 energy code, 2021 plumbing code and 2023 electrical code, required on plans since January 2024. The usual single-family zone is R-1A: lots of at least 9,000 sq ft, house set back 25 ft from the front and rear and 7.5 ft from the sides (12 ft on a corner street side). The house may cover up to half the lot and be up to 42 ft tall. The building permit is about $0.35 per square foot plus a 20% plan-check fee - roughly $1,200 for a 2,400 sq ft home with a 440 sq ft garage, before trade permits. In a mapped flood zone the lowest floor must be at least 1 ft above the base flood level. The city cannot require brick, but an HOA can. Expect an engineer-designed slab on East Texas clay.
